title: Content of a lernapps explainer
description: The content of an app built from the archetype explainer (runtime @lernapps/app-templates), as YAML in src/: the app (src/app.yaml), each chapter (src/<chapter>/chapter.yaml), each page (src/<chapter>/<page>.yaml) and data files (src/data/<name>.yaml). A page is a list of blocks from a closed set; structure comes only from section blocks. The build validates every file against this schema, then what a schema cannot say (order lists complete, depth, languages complete, formulas in the command list), and fails with one line per problem. Every text is for learners, in plain language. A text is a string while German is the app's only language, else a map of texts by language: { de: …, en: … }.

id.description: A stable name, part of the address: lower-case letters, digits and hyphens. Keep it once published, so that links to it keep working.

text.description: A text without formatting: a string while German is the only language of the app, else a map of texts by language ({ de: …, en: … }) with every declared language.

markdown.description: Restricted Markdown, as a text or a map of texts by language: paragraphs, **bold**, *italics*, lists, links and line breaks, formulas as $…$ in the formula command list. No headings (use a section block), no HTML, no images (use a figure block), no code (use a code block), no quotes (use a quote block), no tables (use a table block). A link to a page of the app starts with / and names it from the app's root: /<chapter>/<page>/#<section>.

latex.description: One formula in the LaTeX subset of the formula command list: \frac, \cdot, \times, \div, \%, \text, ^, _, \sqrt, \approx, \pm, \le, \ge, \neq, \, (thin space), parentheses and braces; \ce{…} for chemical equations and \pu{…} for units (mhchem). Written without the $ signs. A map by language only when it has \text{…} that differs by language.

title.description: What the source is, e.g. the title of the article or book.

source.description: Where the app's facts come from.

credit.description: Where a bundled image or a quote comes from: the source (a URL or a citation) and its licence (an SPDX identifier such as CC-BY-SA-4.0, or "gemeinfrei").

source.description: Where it comes from: a URL, the same in every language and shown as a link, or a citation, a text like any other: a string while German is the only language of the app, else a map of texts by language with every declared language, e.g. { de: eigene Zeichnung, en: own drawing }. Each language's page shows its own.

licence.description: Its licence: an SPDX identifier (CC-BY-SA-4.0, CC0-1.0, …), or gemeinfrei for a work in the public domain.

image.description: A bundled image file in src/images/, as a path from src/: images/<name>.svg (or .png, .jpg, .webp).

app.description: src/app.yaml: the app, its languages and the order of its chapters.

title.description: The app's title: the start page's h1 and the title of every page.

intro.description: What the app explains and for whom, under the title of the start page.

languages.description: The languages of the app, German first. Every text is then complete in each of them; each language other than German gets its own page tree below /<language>/.

chapters.description: The order of the chapters: the id of each folder src/<chapter>/, each exactly once. An app with one chapter hides it in the navigation and keeps it in the address.

sources.description: Where the app's facts come from, listed on the start page.

chapter.description: src/<chapter>/chapter.yaml: a chapter and the order of its pages.

summary.description: What the chapter is about, on the chapter's page and in the contents.

pages.description: The order of the pages: the id of each file src/<chapter>/<page>.yaml, each exactly once.

page.description: src/<chapter>/<page>.yaml: a page, its address /<chapter>/<page>/. Its blocks in order; structure by section blocks (h2), with at most one level of sections inside them (h3). Every page has at least one exercise (one of the quiz's question types, or generated), e.g. in a last section Übung.

description.description: One sentence on what the page explains, for search engines and llms.txt.

data.description: src/data/<name>.yaml: a list of records with the same fields, e.g. events with date, title and text. Blocks draw from it by its name (a timeline's data).

formula.description: One formula on its own line, rendered at build to MathML.

figure.description: A figure: drawn from data (draw) or a bundled image (image, with its source and licence), one of the two. It has an alternative text that says what it shows, and a caption that says what to see.

alt.description: What the figure shows, for those who cannot see it.

caption.description: What to see in the figure, under it.

drawing.description: A figure drawn from numbers at build, as inline SVG: hundred-grid (a field of 100 squares, filled of them shaded) or bar (a strip, part of whole shaded, with its percentage).

filled.description: How many of the 100 squares are shaded.

labelledFigure.description: A bundled image with numbered labels at positions and a legend of the labels in order.

alt.description: What the image shows, for those who cannot see it.

caption.description: What to see in the figure.

x.description: From the left edge, in percent of the width.

y.description: From the top edge, in percent of the height.

table.description: A table with a caption. Cells are restricted Markdown without paragraphs.

header.description: The header row: one heading per column.

rowHeaders.description: The first cell of each row heads the row.

timeline.description: Dated events, from the earliest: listed here (events) or the records of a data file (data) with the fields date, title and optional label and text; one of the two.

data.description: The name of a data file src/data/<name>.yaml.

date.description: The date: a year (1789; -44 for 44 BC), a month (1789-07) or a day (1789-07-14).

label.description: The date as the learner reads it, when it differs from the date itself, e.g. um 1500.

title.description: What happened, in a few words.

definition.description: A term and what it means, in place; collected into the app's glossary page, which every term links to.

quote.description: A quotation, quoted exactly, with its origin, source and licence.

text.description: The quotation itself, exactly as written.

origin.description: Who said or wrote it, where and when.

author.description: Who said or wrote it. A name is the same in every language: a string, or a map by language where it differs.

work.description: Where it was said or written: the work, as it is called; a string, or a map by language where its title is translated.

year.description: When: a year, or a text such as um 500 v. Chr.

box.description: A box with a heading (the next level below its place) and blocks: example for a worked example, note for a hint or something to remember. A box holds no sections and no boxes.

section.description: A section: a heading (h2, or h3 inside a section) and its blocks. Its address is #<id>, inside a section #<section>/<id>.

expression.description: An expression of the expression language, e.g. "G * p / 100": numbers (exact fractions), + - * /, parentheses, == != < <= > >=, and, or, not, strings in quotes, record fields (e.year), list index (xs[0]), lists ([1, 2]), and the functions round(x, n), abs, decimals, len, map(xs, field), sortBy(xs, field), reverse, minBy(xs, field), maxBy(xs, field), contains(xs, x), distinct(xs). It may use the variables of given.

literal.description: An item of a list: a number, a string, or a text by language ({ de: …, en: … }).

list.description: A list of items, or the records of a data file: { data: <name> } for src/data/<name>.yaml.

arbitrary.description: How a value of given is drawn, exactly one of: int: [min, max] with a step (default 1); decimal: [min, max] with a step (e.g. 0.1); oneOf: a list to pick one from; pick: how many, from: a list or { data: <name> }, distinct: true for no repeats (pick: 1 gives one item, more give a list); shuffle: a list or { data: <name> } in a random order.

numberCompare.description: The learner types a number. format: integer (no decimals), decimal (decimals, default 2), money (2 decimals, unit €) or percent (unit %); decimals: how many the answer may have; tolerance: how far the learner's number may be off (default 0); unit: shown next to the input.

compare.description: How the learner answers and what counts as right, the quiz's answer kind of the same name: number (the quiz's number question; or { number: { format, decimals, tolerance, unit } }), { choice: <options> } (single choice; the options a list, or an expression giving one), order (the answer a list in the right order; the quiz's ordering), { set: <options> } (multiple choice; the answer the list of right options), pairs (the answer a list of [left, right]; or { pairs: { left: <field>, right: <field> } } for a list of records; the quiz's matching).

generatedFigure.description: A figure drawn from the task's values: hundred-grid with filled, or bar with part and whole, each a number or an expression. Without JavaScript and before the answer it must not show the answer; alt says what it shows, with placeholders ({{G}}; {{figure.filled}} for its own values); a default text by kind otherwise.

generated.description: An exercise drawn from a seed, property-based: given draws the values, where filters them, task is the text with placeholders ({{G}}, {{e.name}}; {{answer}} in the steps) and an optional figure, answer is an expression with its comparator, mistakes are typical wrong answers each with a message saying what went wrong, hint and steps help. A placeholder is always two braces around a declared name or its field, nothing else inside, in prose and in formulas alike ($\frac{{{W}}}{{{G}}}$); one brace is never a placeholder, so in a formula G and {G} are the letter. The build checks that every placeholder names a variable of given (or answer), that no prose has a placeholder with one brace or spaces inside, and that every variable of given is used in a placeholder or in an expression of the figure, answer or mistakes; then it checks it over 200 fixed seeds: where holds in at least 1 of 10 draws; the answer is defined, in its format and passes its comparator; no mistake equals it; the task is the same each time and keeps no placeholder; the figure does not show the answer. Without JavaScript the page shows three worked tasks (seeds 1, 2, 3) with their solution; with JavaScript a live task, Neue Aufgabe, and the deep link ?seed=<n>#<id>.

given.description: The variables and how each is drawn; names of letters, digits and _, e.g. G, p, events.

where.description: Preconditions, each an expression that is true or false; a draw that fails one is drawn again.

text.description: The task, restricted Markdown in one paragraph, with placeholders.

mistakes.description: Typical mistakes: the wrong answer as an expression, and a message (plain text) that says what went wrong.

hint.description: A hint before the answer, restricted Markdown with placeholders.

steps.description: The steps of the solution, restricted Markdown with placeholders and {{answer}}.

vueComponent.description: A Vue single-file component of the app, src/components/<component>.vue, for what no built-in block or generated exercise can express. The build renders it into the page and checks it (what it may do, its test file, and for an exercise, one that emits answered, its logic module <component>.ts); in the browser it hydrates in place. Without JavaScript the page shows its nojs text instead.

component.description: The component's name, in PascalCase: src/components/<component>.vue.

props.description: The component's props, checked against its prop types (defineProps<…>()). A prop of type string is a learner text: a string, or a map by language.

nojs.description: What the component shows and does, for readers without JavaScript, with its content: the labelled diagram described, or the task with its solution. Restricted Markdown, rendered in place; once the component runs, it replaces this text, or keeps it as its caption.
